en.title: Gus Van Sant & Sergei Loznitsa Drop New Films, Plus Carax News
en.summary: This week's streaming arrivals bring a fascinating mix of true crime, historical drama, and suspense. Get ready for cinematic journeys that are as thought-provoking as they are thrilling.
en.body:
The streaming landscape is constantly evolving, and this week brings a fresh wave of compelling cinema to our screens, featuring acclaimed directors and gripping stories. From the late-70s-inspired crime drama of **Gus Van Sant** to the intense legal thriller from **Sergei Loznitsa**, there's something for every discerning viewer.

## A Tale of Two Crimes: Van Sant's 'Dead Man's Wire' and Loznitsa's 'Two Prosecutors'

**Gus Van Sant** returns with **Dead Man's Wire**, a film steeped in the atmospheric hues of the late 1970s, reminiscent of **Kelly Reichardt's** recent work. The film delves into the paradox of the decent criminal, focusing on the true story of **Tony Kiritsis**, brought vividly to life by **Bill Skarsgård**. Skarsgård delivers a performance that commands attention as Kiritsis, a man whose attempt to reclaim a piece of land led him to famously kidnap his mortgage broker in 1977. Van Sant masterfully crafts this narrative, drawing parallels to the chaotic energy of **Dog Day Afternoon**, presenting a stranger-than-fiction fable about good intentions gone awry. It’s a darkly humorous and compelling character study that’s now available on Netflix.

Meanwhile, **Sergei Loznitsa** offers a starkly different, yet equally captivating, cinematic experience with **Two Prosecutors**. This chilling thriller, set to stream in 2026, plunges into the heart of a prison system through the eyes of an idealistic state lawyer, played by **Alexander Kuznetsov**. Summoned by a clandestine note, the young attorney navigates the prison's suspicious authorities to interview an elderly, broken-down Bolshevik. His determination to uncover past injustices clashes with the unyielding apparatus of the state, promising a tense and thought-provoking examination of truth and power.

## More Streaming Gems and Anticipated Releases

Beyond these highlights, the streaming world is also abuzz with other noteworthy additions. **David Mackenzie's** latest, **Fuze**, offers a relentless pace, akin to a feature-length cold open that surges towards its climax. The discovery of World War II ordnance in a quiet English community sets off a chain reaction of panic and action, barely pausing for breath in its 98-minute runtime. This high-octane thriller is available on VOD.

Looking ahead, the cinematic world eagerly anticipates further developments. **Leos Carax**, known for his distinctive style, is reportedly working on projects that hint at his unique vision. While specific details about his upcoming slate are still emerging, the prospect of new work from such a visionary director always generates significant excitement among cinephiles. The Romanian filmmaker **Radu Jude** also continues to impress with films like **Kontinental ‘25**, which grounds its artistic flourishes in everyday reality, a testament to his unique approach to filmmaking.

## What's Next for Film Fans

The release of **Dead Man's Wire** and the upcoming arrival of **Two Prosecutors** underscore the rich diversity of storytelling available to us. Keep an eye on these directors and their future projects as they continue to shape the cinematic conversation. Information regarding the streaming release of **Kontinental ‘25** and other titles mentioned will be updated as it becomes available.

tr.title: Gus Van Sant & Sergei Loznitsa Yeni Filmleri, Carax Haberi
tr.summary: Bu hafta gelen akış içeriği, gerçek bir suç, tarihsel drama ve gerilim ile dolu ilginç bir karışım sunuyor. Görsel yolculuklar hem düşündürücü hem de heyecan verici.
tr.body:
Akış ortamı sürekli değişiyor ve bu hafta yeni, çekici bir dizi film ve yönetmen geldi. **Gus Van Sant**'ın 70'lerin sonuna kadar ilham alan suç draması **Dead Man's Wire** ve **Sergei Loznitsa**'nın yoğun bir yasal gerilim filmi **Two Prosecutors** ile her tür izleyiciye birşeyler sunuyor.

## A Two Crimes: Van Sant'in 'Dead Man's Wire' ve Loznitsa'nın 'Two Prosecutors'

**Gus Van Sant** **Dead Man's Wire** ile geri döndü, bu film 70'lerin sonuna kadar ilham alan atmosferik renglerle dolu. **Kelly Reichardt**'in recent çalışması gibi. Film, iyi bir suçlu olmanın paradoksu ile ilgilidir, **Tony Kiritsis**'in gerçek hikayesini ele alır, **Bill Skarsgård** tarafından canlandırılır. Skarsgård, Kiritsis'i canlandırırken, bir performans sergiler. Kiritsis, 1977'de mortgage brokerini famous olarak kaçırmak için bir parça arazi geri alma girişiminde bulundu. Van Sant, bu anlatıyı ustaca yaratır, **Dog Day Afternoon**'un kaotik enerjisini sunar, iyi niyetin yanlış giden bir fabeli sunar. Bu, şimdi Netflix'te bulunan, karanlık bir komedi ve çekici bir karakter çalışmasıdır.

Aynı zamanda **Sergei Loznitsa**, **Two Prosecutors** ile tamamen farklı, ama eşit derecede çekici bir sinematik deneyimi sunar. Bu gerilim filmi, 2026'da akışa gelecek, bir idealist devlet avukatının gözlerinden bir hapishane sisteminin içine girer. Avukat, **Alexander Kuznetsov** tarafından canlandırılır. Bir gizli nota ile çağrılan genç hukukçu, bir yaşlı, çökmüş Bolşevik'i interview etmek için hapishanenin şüpheli yetkilileri ile karşı karşıya gelir. Gerçeği bulma niyeti, devletin kaba güçleri ile çatışır, gerçek ve güç arasındaki gerilim dolu bir incelemeyi sunar.

## Daha Fazla Akış İpuçları ve Beklenen Çıkmalar

Bu yükseklights'ın ötesinde, akış dünyası da diğer önemli eklemelerle dolu. **David Mackenzie**'in son çalışması **Fuze**, bir özellik uzunluğunda soğuk açılış gibi, bir zincir reaksiyonu ile sona erer. Dünya Savaşı'ndan kalma bir İngiliz köyünde, bir zincir reaksiyonu başlar. Bu, 98 dakika süren, bir dizi panik ve eylem ile doludur. Bu yüksek-octane gerilim filmi VOD'da mevcuttur.

Geleceğe bakıldığında, sinema dünyası, yeni projeleri bekliyor. **Leos Carax**, kendine özgü stili ile tanınır. Beklenen projeleri ile ilgili, henüz belirli ayrıntılar ortaya çıkmadı, ancak bu tür bir vizyoner yönetmenden yeni bir çalışma, sinemaseverler arasında büyük heyecan yaratır. **Radu Jude** de, **Kontinental ‘25** gibi filmleri ile sinemaseverleri etkiler. Bu film, her günkü gerçeklikle sanatlı birleşimini sunar, **Radu Jude**'ün benzersiz yaklaşımlarının bir kanıtıdır.

## Filmseverler İçin Gelecek

**Dead Man's Wire**'in çıkışı ve **Two Prosecutors**'un gelecek akışı, bize sunulan zengin hikaye çeşitliliğini vurgular. Bu yönetmenlerin ve gelecekteki projelerinin izlemeye devam edin, sinema konuşmasını şekillendirecekler.

es.title: Gus Van Sant y Sergei Loznitsa presentan sus últimas películas, junto con noticias sobre Carax
es.summary: Esta semana llegan a las plataformas de streaming una fascinante mezcla de crimen, drama histórico y suspense. Prepárense para viajes cinematográficos que son a la vez pensativos y emocionantes.
es.body:
La escena de streaming está en constante evolución, y esta semana trae una nueva oleada de cine atractivo a nuestras pantallas, con directores aclamados y historias apasionantes. Desde el drama de crimen de los setenta de **Gus Van Sant** hasta el thriller legal intenso de **Sergei Loznitsa**, hay algo para cada espectador discernente.

## Un cuento de dos crímenes: Van Sant's 'Dead Man's Wire' y Loznitsa's 'Two Prosecutors'

**Gus Van Sant** regresa con **Dead Man's Wire**, una película sumida en los tonos atmosféricos de finales de la década de 1970, reminiscente del trabajo reciente de **Kelly Reichardt**. La película explora el paradoja del criminal decente, centrada en la historia verdadera de **Tony Kiritsis**, llevada vividamente a la vida por **Bill Skarsgård**. Skarsgård ofrece una actuación que llama la atención como Kiritsis, un hombre cuyo intento de reclamar una pieza de tierra lo llevó a famosamente secuestrar a su corredor hipotecario en 1977. Van Sant maestra la narrativa, trazando paralelos con la energía caótica de **Dog Day Afternoon**, presentando una fábula más extraña que la realidad sobre intenciones buenas que salen mal. Es una historia oscura y humorísticamente atractiva y una fascinante exploración del carácter que ya está disponible en Netflix.

Mientras tanto, **Sergei Loznitsa** ofrece una experiencia cinematográfica completamente diferente, aunque igualmente cautivadora, con **Two Prosecutors**. Este thriller aterrador, que se estrenará en 2026, se adentra en el corazón de un sistema penitenciario a través de los ojos de un abogado estatal idealista, interpretado por **Alexander Kuznetsov**. Convocado por una nota clandestina, el joven abogado navega por las autoridades sospechosas de la prisión para entrevistar a un anciano y desmoronado bolchevique. Su determinación para descubrir injusticias pasadas se enfrenta con el aparato inquebrantable del Estado, prometiendo una tensa y reflexiva exploración de la verdad y el poder.

## Más tesoros en streaming y lanzamientos anticipados

Más allá de estos destellos, el mundo de streaming también está bullendo con otras adiciones destacadas. **David Mackenzie's** más reciente, **Fuze**, ofrece un ritmo incesante, similar a un apertura de largometraje que surge hacia su clímax. La descubierta de armas de la Segunda Guerra Mundial en una comunidad inglesa tranquila desencadena una reacción en cadena de pánico y acción, apenas deteniéndose para respirar en su runtime de 98 minutos. Este thriller de alta intensidad está disponible en VOD.

Mientras tanto, el mundo cinematográfico ansia con impaciencia más noticias. **Leos Carax**, conocido por su estilo distintivo, está trabajando en proyectos que sugieren su visión única. Aunque los detalles específicos sobre su próxima producción están aún emergiendo, la perspectiva de nuevos trabajos de un director tan visionario siempre genera gran entusiasmo entre los cineastas.

El cineasta rumano **Radu Jude** también sigue impresionando con películas como **Kontinental ‘25**, que funda sus florituras artísticas en la realidad cotidiana, testimonio de su enfoque único en la creación cinematográfica.

## Próximos pasos para los amantes del cine

La llegada de **Dead Man's Wire** y la próxima llegada de **Two Prosecutors** destacan la rica diversidad de historias disponibles para nosotros. Mantengan un ojo en estos directores y sus futuros proyectos mientras siguen moldeando la conversación cinematográfica. Se actualizará la información sobre el lanzamiento de **Kontinental ‘25** y otros títulos mencionados a medida que se vuelva disponible.

content_raw: Each week we highlight the noteworthy titles that have recently hit streaming platforms in the United States. Check out this week’s selections below and past round-ups  here . Dead Man’s Wire (Gus Van Sant) Gus Van Sant returns with  Dead Man’s Wire , a movie shot in the same late-70s hues as Kelly Reichardt’s recent gem  The Mastermind , and likewise concerned with unlawful men and the paradox of a decent criminal. Van Sant’s movie, however, is far more willing to deliver on genre tropes than Reichardt’s marvelous subversion. Bill Skarsgård eats great swathes of scenery as the very real Tony Kiritsis, a man who kidnapped his mortgage broker in 1977 after failing to make payment on a potentially lucrative plot of land. Van Sant imagines this tale in a way that echoes  Dog Day Afternoon : an unhinged and stranger-than-fiction fable about good intentions gone wrong. It’s kind of a hoot. – Rory O. ( full review ) Where to Stream: Netflix Fuze (David Mackenzie) David Mackenzie gets the opening credits out of the way as soon as we sit down to watch his latest film  Fuze . A majority of the 98 minutes which follow are akin to a feature-length cold open surging at breakneck speed to its own climax. When the discovery of a WWII ordinance during construction in a residential English community sends everyone running around, it takes half that time before there’s even a brief pause in the action. – Jared M. ( full review ) Where to Stream: VOD Kontinental ‘25 (Radu Jude) “The id grows tedious,” art critic Jackson Arn wrote recently, “when left to speak too freely.” The Romanian filmmaker Radu Jude keeps his in check by grounding flourishes in pure mundanity. Near the end of  Kontinental ’25 , an ex-professor, Orsolya (Eszter Tompa), and her former student, Fred (Adonis Tanța), sit by an anti-communist resistance monument in Cluj and watch a horrific video of a drone attack on a Russian soldier. Having found the dead body of a man she evicted earlier that day, Orsolya, who now works as a bailiff, is looking to blow off some steam. They move uphill and Fred––whose delivery bag is plastered with Romanian flags, so as not to be confused with immigrant gig workers––serenades her. Next, they have sex in the bushes. The film up to this point has been awash with ideas and vaguely apocalyptic images: Roman ruins, a robot dog, a dinosaur park, zoomed-in footage of the Hindenburg disaster, a scene from Robert Aldrich’s atomic-era nightmare  Kiss Me Deadly . This should all be  a lot , but somehow Jude keeps it together. – Rory O.
